correctness.rationale: Full 14-count profile is equivalent to the explicitly invertible five run parameters; necessary lower/upper and two boundary indicator constraints follow from sum-of-run lengths and the Dyck prefix property. Sorting eligible up-runs decreasing and down-runs increasing proves a Dyck representative for each feasible tuple by prefix-majorization. Exactly three squared-range contributions sum to the cubic polynomial for all m>=1; endpoint m=1 is explicitly handled. Both standalone finite verification programs passed on actual package paths; no infinite assertion is inferred from their finite tests.

evidence: The general k-Abelian articles define full-factor-count equality and discuss all-word class growth or singleton sizes; their statements do not evaluate Dyck-restricted joint support.
Existing published unrestricted binary linear-three-gram censuses grow quartically, but their all-binary profile universe does not indicate which observed vectors have Dyck representatives.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General polynomial-growth assertions and unrestricted factor-spectrum enumerators do not determine the much smaller Dyck feasible subset or the boundary-flag inequalities. Neither a theorem of the restricted subset nor an implication preserving Dyck path balance was located.

evidence: The 2015 paper fixes one substring and remembers all its occurrence positions; these are neither the same invariant nor enough to enumerate the simultaneous histogram vectors for all eight trigrams.
The all-word 2013 and 2016 theorems establish broad equivalence properties without Dyck-specific boundary feasibility constraints.
A116731 identifies a different enumerated object and its cubic size, but supplies no proof that the five-parameter Dyck profile set has that cardinality.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Even the conjunction of those checked results leaves open which joint profiles are Dyck-feasible; Steps 1–3 of RESULT.md prove that by a nontrivial run-sorting majorization construction, and Step 4 counts the support. This is not claimed as an independent new integer sequence.

evidence: In a Dyck word, 3-Abelian equivalence equals equality of all 14 linear overlapping short-factor counts; a joint count, not positions of occurrences of a chosen factor.
The 2015 Dyck paper defines equivalence by occurrence positions for one fixed pattern rather than equality of all simultaneous short-factor multiplicities.
A116731 has the identical polynomial but enumerates a class of permutations.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The exact polynomial alone is already covered numerically. An equivalence would require a construction connecting a known counted class to attainable Dyck 3-Abelian observations or a full factor-histogram theorem. Neither appears in the inspected material; the present explicit feasibility theorem is the distinguishing claim.

evidence: OEIS A116731 explicitly lists 1,2,5,12,25,46,77,... and the exact formula (n^3-3n^2+5n)/3, attributed as a formula in 2006.
OEIS assigns the numbers to avoidance of several permutation patterns; it does not describe Dyck 3-Abelian observations or feasible five-parameter signatures.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The count and generating function are numerically known; these are reported as a new structural realization and reconstruction interpretation only, rather than as new numbers. No asserted novelty attaches to the OEIS polynomial.

originality.rationale: No inspected previous statement, including the most directly related 2015 Dyck fixed-pattern paper or general 2013/2016 k-Abelian papers, gives the simultaneous Dyck 3-Abelian vector support and constructive five-parameter classification. The exact numerical sequence is already OEIS A116731 for a distinct permutation class; the original claim is explicitly the Dyck-profile realization theorem and reconstruction interpretation, not discovery of the polynomial. Plausible unindexed earlier interpretations remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed papers or a later follow-up may already contain an equivalent Dyck 3-Abelian realization theorem.
The 2011 single-pattern Dyck string-enumeration full text was not inspected; only its public abstract was checked.
The count is numerically identical to a long-known permutation-avoidance sequence, so priority is strictly limited to the distinct Dyck-support interpretation and proof.

value.rationale: Complete realizable short-factor profile support of the globally balanced Dyck language is a natural reconstruction invariant; the five-parameter necessary-and-sufficient criterion supplies explicit representatives and the exact all-length zero-error code size. The result is more than the already-known cubic OEIS number: it gives a fresh constrained-language classification absent from the compared literature. No fiber-size or general channel capacity result is claimed.
